tutorial.title: PUT Requests
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to use a PUT request to send data to a server

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
PUT is a request method used to update or replace a resource on the server.

Unlike POST, which typically creates new resources, PUT is used when the client sends data to modify an existing resource.

lessons.title: PUT
lessons.interactiveContent:
PUT is a request method that we use to update existing data on the server, like modifying an existing course Mimo wants to revise.

Make sure to pick PUT.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Update the existing course 10 on mimo.org.

Make sure to pick PUT.

lessons.title: PUT URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
PUT relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource the new data is related to.

Make sure to pick mimo.org.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PUT relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource the new data is related to.

Target course 10 in the courses resource on mimo.org.

Make sure to pick mimo.org, followed by courses.

lessons.title: PUT URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
This PUT request's URL shows that an existing course should be updated or replaced under courses.

Make sure to pick /courses, followed by /10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the resource path to target the existing course with ID 10 under courses.

Make sure to pick /courses, followed by /10.

lessons.title: PUT URL Query Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
In a PUT request, the payload contains the full updated data for the resource being modified.

We send the entire updated resource, as it replaces the current one, meaning missing fields may be removed.

Make sure to pick {, followed by }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In a PUT request, the payload contains the full updated data for the resource being modified.

You send the entire updated resource, as it replaces the current one, meaning missing fields may be removed.

Keep both title and languages in the replacement JSON object.

Make sure to pick {, followed by languages, and finally }.

lessons.title: Question: PUT
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we use PUT requests for?

For updating or replacing existing data on the serverFor retrieving data from the server

For updating or replacing existing data on the server.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Course 10 already exists, and the server should replace it with fully updated data. What is the PUT request doing?

Updating or replacing course 10 on the serverRetrieving course 10 without changing itCreating a new course without identifying an existing course

Updating or replacing course 10 on the server.

lessons.title: Question: PUT URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does the browser know where to send the data in the PUT request?

Through the server address in the request's URLBy reading the data that the request is sending

Through the server address in the request's URL.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A PUT request uses https://api.mimo.org/users/937. What tells the browser which server receives the data?

The api.mimo.org server address in the URLThe username and email values in the request bodyThe user ID 937 without the rest of the URL

The api.mimo.org server address in the URL.

lessons.title: Question: PUT URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Looking at this URL, what might the data we're sending be related to?

An update to an existing article A new article submitted by someone

An update to an existing article.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The URL ends in /article/458 and the title says [Revised]. What operation does this request represent?

An update that replaces existing article 458A new article with no existing article IDAn update to comment 458 on an article

An update that replaces existing article 458.

lessons.title: Example: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an HTTP request method that updates data from a server.

Make sure to pick PUT.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Replace the full existing article 112 on fakenews.com with updated data.

Make sure to pick PUT, followed by fakenews.com.

lessons.title: Example: PUT URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send a PUT request to a server at fakenews.com.

Make sure to type PUT.

lessons.title: Example: PUT URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Through the PUT request's URL, let the server know which article to update.

Make sure to pick / followed by article and then /, 458.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Target article 458 on fakenews.com, using its ID in the resource path.

Make sure to pick /, followed by article, /, and finally 458.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
In a PUT request, do you send only the data you want to change or the entire updated resource?

You send the entire updated resourceYou only send the data you want to change

You send the entire updated resource.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A user has username and email. A PUT request changes the username. What should its body contain?

The updated username and the unchanged emailOnly the updated usernameNo body because the username belongs in the URL

The updated username and the unchanged email.

lessons.title: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
PUT requests look very similar to POST requests in Express.

Make sure to pick put.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PUT requests look very similar to POST requests in Express.

Make sure to pick put, followed by users.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like with POST requests, we define the endpoint for PUT requests as well.

However, we must also include the specific resource identifier in the URL to specify which resource should be updated.

Make sure to pick / followed by users and then /, :id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Like with POST requests, we define the endpoint for PUT requests as well.

However, we must also include the specific resource identifier in the URL to specify which resource should be updated.

Make sure to pick /, followed by users, /, :id, and finally res.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
PUT requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be updated.

We use req.params.id to unpack a route parameter with the name id.

Make sure to pick req followed by . and then params, ., id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PUT requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be updated.

Use req.params and the parameter name from the route to identify the user.

Make sure to pick req, followed by ., params, ., and finally id.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like POST requests, PUT requests also contain data in their request body.

In a PUT request, we send the entire updated resource, as it replaces the current one, meaning missing fields may be removed.

Make sure to pick req, followed by .body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Like POST requests, PUT requests also contain data in their request body.

In a PUT request, you send the entire updated resource, as it replaces the current one, meaning missing fields may be removed.

Log the stored user ID, then read and log the submitted replacement body.

Make sure to pick userId, followed by req, and finally .body.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
To allow accessing the body, we need to tell our express app to use express.json, a built-in middleware.

Make sure to pick express.json().
lessons.hardModeContent:
To access the body, tell your Express app to use express.json, a built-in middleware.

Make sure to pick use, followed by express.json().

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to access the passed data, we parse it. As soon as we've done that, we can access and work with the data in the request body.

Make sure to pick username, followed by email.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To access the passed data, parse it. You can then access and work with the data in the request body.

Read the username and email from the parsed body and log each under its matching label.

Make sure to pick requestData, followed by username, and finally email.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Similar to other methods, we can and should send back a response.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., and finally send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Similar to other methods, we can and should send back a response.

Make sure to pick req, followed by res, ., and finally send.

lessons.title: a
lessons.interactiveContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and a new element is created or added to the database is 200 OK.

Make sure to pick ., followed by status(200).
lessons.hardModeContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and a new element is created or added to the database is 200 OK.

Make sure to pick params, followed by ., and finally status(200).

lessons.title: a - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We first specify the HTTP status code and then send the response body to the client.

Make sure to pick . followed by status(200) and then ., send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We first specify the HTTP status code and then send the response body to the client.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., status(200), ., and finally send.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
To update an existing user, we might require certain parameters, such as an email, to be sent with the request.

If we have all the data and can add the user, we send 200 OK. If data is missing, we send 400 Bad Request with an error message.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by 200.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To replace an existing user, require an email in the submitted body.

After replacement succeeds, send 200 OK. If email is missing, send 400 Bad Request with an error message.

Make sure to pick put, followed by 400, and finally 200.

lessons.title: PUT Headers
lessons.interactiveContent:
A PUT request has headers providing extra context, like Content-Type which tells us the format of the request body.

Make sure to pick Content-Type:, followed by application/json.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A PUT request has headers providing extra context, like Content-Type which tells us the format of the request body.

Make sure to pick Content-Type:, followed by application/json.

lessons.title: PUT Headers 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
You can see that this PUT request's body Content-Type is application/json, the most common content type.

Make sure to pick application, followed by /, and finally json.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Host identifies the server. Content-Type describes the body format; JSON uses application/json.

Match the headers to the shown server and JSON body format.

Make sure to pick Host, followed by Content-Type, and finally application/json.

lessons.title: Question: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where do PUT requests store the data they send to the server?

In the request bodyOnly in the URL, as query parameter values

In the request body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A PUT request sends a new title and languages list for course 10. Where does this data go?

In the request bodyOnly after /courses/10 as query parameter valuesInside the Content-Type header

Make sure to pick In the request body.

lessons.title: Example: PUT Body JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a PUT endpoint to update a specific user.

Make sure to pick app followed by . and then put, "/users/:id".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create a PUT endpoint under /users with a route parameter named id.

Make sure to pick app, followed by ., put, and finally "/users/:id".

lessons.title: Question: POST Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What might this PUT request send to the server?

An update to a comment to an articleA user's data, including username and description

An update to a comment to an article.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The path is /article/112/comment/49, and the body has comment text and an author. What is being updated?

Comment 49 on article 112The profile of user 49A brand-new comment with no comment ID

Make sure to pick Comment 49 on article 112.

lessons.title: Question: POST Body JSON
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's one popular option for formatting a PUT request's data?

JSONHTTP

Make sure to pick JSON.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A PUT body is written as { "title": "TypeScript" }. Which format does this use?

JSONHTTPURL

Make sure to pick JSON.

lessons.title: Question: POST Headers
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will the status code be if all the required data is provided and the request is successful?

200 OK400 Bad Request

200 OK.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request provides username but omits email. Which response does this handler send?

200 OK with User created400 Bad Request with Email is required404 Not Found because the user ID is missing from the body

400 Bad Request with Email is required.

lessons.title: Example: POST Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the correct codes.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by 200.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set the correct codes.

Make sure to pick 400, followed by is, and finally 200.

lessons.title: Example: POST Headers
lessons.interactiveContent:
Send back a response along with the correct status code.

Make sure to pick res followed by . and then status, (, 200, ), ., send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Send back a response along with the correct status code.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., status, (, 200, ), ., and finally send.

lessons.title: Question: POST Headers 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does a PUT request's Content-Type header tell us?

The format of the data we're sending to the serverThe format of the data in the server's database

The format of the data we're sending to the server.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The sequence now shows a POST request.

Regardless of the request method, what does Content-Type: application/json say about the comment body?

The comment body is sent in JSON formatThe server must store every comment in JSON formatThe request URL is written in JSON format

The comment body is sent in JSON format.
